_meta.how_to_regression_diff: Re-run cases (npm run check:golden pep). Diff for QUALITY not exact match: HTTP 200, no truncation. FOCUSED REBUILD (2026-09-05): installed from an owner-supplied rewrite (audit/tool-notes/PEP-NOTES.md) that reduces the prior FULL V2 REWRITE's five modes (Right Now/Prioritize/Week/Patterns/Adapt, 17 actions) down to ONE loop across 3 actions: generate (Right Now menu), just-do-this (single suggestion, no menu), reflect (log what happened). Prioritize/Week/Patterns/Adapt/Shared menu/Match/build-a-plan are GONE, not renamed — do not resurrect their schema keys chasing a 'completeness' instinct. New schema: generate={read,top_pick:{activity,why_it_fits,first_step,duration,done_when},alternatives:[{activity,why_it_fits,duration}],history_note}; just-do-this={activity,why_it_fits,first_step,duration,done_when,history_note}; reflect={reflection,history_observation}. LIVE-CAUGHT BUG, fixed same day: the SYSTEM prompt's own 'avoid absolutes about effort' rule listed the banned phrases ('zero effort, no attention, no decisions, completely passive') as a literal example list, and the model echoed them back near-verbatim on the FIRST test call ('This requires zero setup, zero decisions, and zero physical effort') — the model was handed a copyable bad-phrase template and copied it. Fixed by describing the constraint without listing the banned words as an example set. The validateResult() regex backstop ALSO missed this on the first pass — its 260-char/2-sentence cap (meant to spare a long paragraph from being nuked over one incidental match) let a 3-sentence field with a genuine, repeated 'zero X' violation straight through; raised to 400 chars/3 sentences. Both fixes verified together: re-ran the exact failing input, output came back clean ('asks very little... no setup, no goal, no output' — describing fit, not claiming zero demand). The generate-low-energy-evening-screens case captured here IS that exact regression input — re-running it and finding a 'zero setup/effort/decisions/attention' phrase anywhere in the output is the bug back. DO NOT reintroduce: any of the removed modes' schema keys; a prompt rule that lists banned phrases as a literal copyable example set (describe the constraint, don't hand over the phrase); the tight 260/2 validateResult cap (400/3 is the corrected value). SECOND live-caught bug, same day: a visitor screenshot showed the top_pick activity title rendered one word per line in a collapsed column — root cause was 'duration' holding a full clause ('20 minutes lying still, leaving 10 minutes to sit up, reorient, and prepare for your call.') instead of a short time span; the flex row's whitespace-nowrap duration span demanded its full single-line width and starved the title's share of the row. Fixed at three layers: (1) prompt now explicitly caps duration at ~4 words with an example; (2) a shortenDuration() backstop in validateResult() extracts the leading time span or cuts at the first clause break, deterministically, regardless of prompt compliance; (3) the frontend Activity card gives the title flex-1 min-w-0 and caps the duration span at max-w-[40%] instead of an unbounded whitespace-nowrap sibling, so even an unexpectedly long duration can no longer collapse the title. All three cases here were re-captured after the fix — every duration value is now a short span (e.g. '10–15 minutes'). DO NOT reintroduce whitespace-nowrap on that duration span, and do not let 'duration' drift back into a descriptive clause.

input.context: Been staring at screens all day, doom-scrolling between meetings. A hike sounds awful right now.

output.read: You've had a full day of screen-based, passive scrolling with very little physical movement or deliberate choice. At 2/10, something that asks almost nothing of you and gets you off screens fits best.

top_pick.activity: Lie down with your eyes closed and put on something audio-only — a podcast, an album, a radio station, anything you can pick in under a minute
top_pick.why_it_fits: No screen, very little setup, and you only need to make one small choice upfront — what to play. After that, nothing is asked of you. Lying flat also changes your physical position from a day spent sitting at screens, with barely any effort required to do it.
top_pick.first_step: Grab your phone or speaker, pick something audio without overthinking it, lie down wherever is comfortable, and press play.
top_pick.done_when: When the 15 minutes are up, or whenever you feel like stopping — whichever comes first.

alternatives.activity: Sit somewhere that isn't your usual screen spot and do nothing in particular — look out a window, look at a wall, let your mind wander
Handle one small physical thing in your home — fold something, throw something away, fill a glass of water
alternatives.why_it_fits: After a day that was entirely screen-based, something with your hands and body requires very little thought but shifts what you're doing. One item only — no list, no project.

input.context: Meeting in 10 minutes and I cannot decide anything else right now.

output.activity: Sit still and let your eyes rest on one neutral spot
output.first_step: Put anything in your hands down, find a neutral spot on the wall or desk, and let your gaze land there.
output.done_when: When you hear or notice it is time to join the meeting.
output.history_note: No previous attempts on record, so this suggestion is based only on what you shared right now.

input.note: Felt better once I was outside

output.reflection: You rated this 8/10 for helpfulness and reported a 3-point lift in energy — and noted feeling better once you were outside. One attempt worth keeping in mind for low-energy moments.
